cards.explanation: The answer is a spirit keeps seizing him. The father says it himself: “A spirit keeps seizing him, and he screams abruptly.” He goes on to say it throws the boy into convulsions so that he foams at the mouth (Luke 9:39). That's a dad who describes exactly what he's seen, no sugarcoating. Hold onto that, friends, because it sets up everything Jesus does next.

The answer is Jesus' disciples. The father tells Jesus, “I begged Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable” (Luke 9:40). He doesn't dress it up or soften it. He just reports what happened, straight to Jesus' face. Honest to the bone, that man.

The answer is “Bring your son here.” After His “How long must I remain with you…” line, Jesus tells the father, “Bring your son here” (Luke 9:41). No speech about it. Jesus calls the boy to Himself. Short and clear, and the father has his answer.

The answer is that Jesus rebukes the spirit and heals the boy. Even after the boy is slammed to the ground, Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit and heals him (Luke 9:42). Jesus does it Himself, right there. The spirit slammed him down, and Jesus still wasn't done. I think the dad needed to see exactly that.

The answer is True. Luke says Jesus healed the boy “…and gave him back to his father” (Luke 9:42). Think about who that father is: a man who called this boy his only child. I think this is the line to sit with for a second, friends. The boy is well, and Jesus gives him back to his dad.

The answer is False. The disciples do not understand it. Luke says, “But they did not understand this statement.” It was veiled from them so they could not comprehend it. And they were afraid to ask Jesus about it, so the confusion just sat there (Luke 9:45).

The answer is which of them would be the greatest. Luke says an argument started among the disciples “…as to which of them would be the greatest” (Luke 9:46). Jesus had just told them something heavy about the Son of Man. And the next thing you know, they're comparing rankings. I'd like to say I've never seen that kind of thing, but I'd be lying.

The answer is a little child. Jesus, knowing the thoughts of their hearts, “…had a little child stand beside Him” (Luke 9:47). He doesn't start with a lecture. He sets a child right there where everyone can see. Then He speaks to them about welcoming that child in His name.

The answer is Jesus. He says, “Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me…” Then He adds, “…and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me” (Luke 9:48). So welcoming that child in His name connects straight to Him. That's a big deal for a little child standing right beside Him, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “For whoever is the least among all of you, he is the greatest” (Luke 9:48). That flips the whole argument over. They were fighting over who ranks first, and He answers with the least. I picture some very quiet disciples after that one.

The answer is driving out demons. John, one of Jesus' disciples, says, “we saw someone driving out demons in Your name…” (Luke 9:49). The man was doing it in Jesus' name, and John says that right up front. So the disciples spotted a man doing the very thing they had struggled with earlier. And John goes on to say what they did about it.

The answer is that he was not traveling with them. John gives the reason himself: “…we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us” (Luke 9:49). The man was driving out demons in Jesus' name, and the problem was that he wasn't with their group. That's the whole complaint, friends. Jesus answers it in the very next verse.

The answer is “against.” Jesus says, “Do not stop him, for whoever is not against you is for you” (Luke 9:50). The word is “against,” and it's a short one. The man was driving out demons in Jesus' name. So Jesus tells the disciples to leave him alone.
